wu: Warm-up: 'Two Truths and a Lie' - Students write three sentences about Halloween: two true (e.g., 'I like pumpkin pie'), one false (e.g., 'I am a vampire'). In pairs, they guess the lie.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Halloween Pictionary' - Teacher draws Halloween words, students guess.
Alternative 2: 'Word Association' - Teacher says 'Halloween', students say related words.
pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of Halloween items (bat, witch, pumpkin, ghost). Model sentences: 'There is a bat.' 'There are two ghosts.' Check understanding by asking 'What is in the picture?' and having students repeat.
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'Spooky Story' - Tell a short story using target vocabulary, e.g., 'In the room, there is a big pumpkin and a black cat.'
Alternative 2: 'Realia Hunt' - Hide small Halloween toys in the classroom, students find them and say 'There is a...'
prac: Guided practice: 'Spooky Room Description Pairs' - Student A describes a picture with 'there is/there are' (e.g., 'There is a spider on the wall. There are three candles.'). Student B draws. Swap roles.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Memory Game' - Students take turns adding to a spooky room description (e.g., 'There is a ghost.' 'There is a ghost and a spider.')
Alternative 2: 'Find the Differences' - Students compare two similar spooky room pictures and say 'There is a... in picture 1 but not in picture 2.'
ls: Listening slot: Students listen to a description of a spooky room (e.g., 'There is a black cat. There are three bats. There is a big pumpkin.'). They draw what they hear. Teacher checks drawings for comprehension.
re: Reactivation game: 'Halloween Charades' - Students act out Halloween words (witch, ghost, spider) while others guess. After the break, this brings the vocabulary back physically.
prod: Production task: 'Spooky Room Project' - In pairs, students design a spooky room on paper. They write three sentences using 'there is/there are' to describe it. They present their room to the class.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text about Halloween (e.g., 'Halloween is on October 31st. People wear costumes. There are pumpkins and ghosts.'). They answer 2-3 simple questions (e.g., 'What date is Halloween?'). Then, they write three 'there is/there are' sentences about their own spooky room.
st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'Five Little Pumpkins' song. Close with 'Today we learned Halloween vocabulary and how to describe a spooky room with there is/there are. Thank you, class!'
g: Students mark Halloween words on their bingo cards as the teacher calls them.
In teams, race to write as many Halloween words as possible in 2 minutes.
Students add one sentence to a collaborative spooky story.
Students draw Halloween words for their team to guess.
Teacher hides flashcards, students find and say 'There is a...'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a longer description of a spooky room with five sentences.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with Halloween vocabulary to write their sentences.
hw: Homework option 1: Write a short paragraph: 'What independence means to me.'
Homework option 2: Bring one Halloween-themed word to teach the class next week.
Homework option 3: Draw a spooky room and label the items in English.
tip: Use the local context of Independence Day (18 November 1955) to connect Halloween's spooky fun with themes of history and national identity, making the lesson culturally relevant for Moroccan learners.
